expected_outcomes: David Clarke’s Holloway ISA is included in report scope.
Susan Clarke’s Holloway ISA is included in report scope.
The joint Holloway GIA is included in report scope.
The joint GIA is counted once, not twice because it appears under both holders.
David’s ISA valuation is 61,000 GBP.
Susan’s ISA valuation is 58,500 GBP.
The date attached to David’s database ISA valuation is 2026-04-30.
The date attached to Susan’s database ISA valuation is 2026-04-30.
If the historical GIA database valuation is reported, it is identified as 40,000 GBP dated 2026-03-15 rather than as a current live value.
The later live GIA observation of a little over 45,000 GBP is disclosed, or explicitly described as an unresolved observation. Omitting it entirely does not meet this outcome.
The later live GIA observation is associated with 2026-05-14 when reported.
The live GIA observation retains the qualification a little over rather than becoming an exact 45,000 GBP value.
The agreed action is to disinvest the joint GIA in full.
The GIA proceeds are to be split equally between the two existing ISAs.
The report does not invent exact ISA contribution amounts.
The report does not independently claim that remaining ISA allowances have been verified.
The agreed risk score is 5.
The agreed risk description is balanced.
The initial charge is 0%.
The report preserves that neither client currently needs portfolio income.
The ongoing platform charge is identified as requiring confirmation.
The ongoing advice charge is identified as requiring confirmation.
Potential CGT implications of the GIA disposal are included.
The tax discussion refers to the annual exempt amount.
The report does not invent a tax estimate.
The report does not invent acquisition costs or calculated gains.
The report does not invent a numerical capital-gains exemption.
The irrelevant holiday discussion is omitted; calling it irrelevant while including it does not meet this outcome.
